description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
2 blocks, no LayerNorm: attention fetches digits and sums signed residues per prime; ReLU bumps detect divisibility; 1/p^2 votes pick the smallest divisor; a tiny copy vote handles primes.
As v1 but integer domination votes: vote(p) = 1 + max total vote of larger primes that can co-divide n, so the smallest divisor always wins.
Single attention layer: a 6th head of block 1 does the prime-case digit copy, so block 2 is MLP-only; digit and key slots share one head dimension.
Removes the ZERO vote slot: at the two leading output positions the hundreds votes are gated onto digit 0, cutting the bump-to-vote fan-out from 4 to 3.
Sensitivity test on v4: attention sharpness BETA lowered from 10 to 5, to see whether near-hard digit selection is really required.
Sensitivity test on v4: BETA=7, bracketing the sharpness threshold between the failing BETA=5 and the working BETA=10.
BETA back to 10. Each prime scales its residue row by the multiplier m that narrows the range of S_p the most, so fewer multiples need a bump.
Multipliers reverted (only 8 fewer bumps). Each prime writes one readable flag f_p; block 2 has one gated vote unit per prime per answer digit, removing the 24 vote-slot dimensions.
Restores the final LayerNorm from the default architecture; it shifts and scales all logits alike, so it cannot change the argmax.
Fixes v9: LayerNorm's mean shift pushed digit logits below the zero logit of '=', so '=' won. The '=' logit now reads the average digit logit, which a leading digit always beats.
Ablation on flags_v8 (final LayerNorm dropped again): trial divisors only up to 97, to measure the accuracy-versus-size trade-off.
Ablation on flags_v8: trial divisors up to 199, a second point on the accuracy-versus-size curve.
Back to all 65 primes; GATE reduced from 2^22 to 2^18, just above the largest possible total vote, keeping the weights' dynamic range tight.
Removes the GATE constant: block 2 units are pure AND gates relu(f_p + pos_t - 1) on booleans, and the vote weights move to fc2.
Thresholded AND relu(2 f_p + pos_t - 2) ignores flags below 0.5, tested at BETA=5 to see whether it repairs the fragility seen in beta5_v5.
Thresholded AND at BETA=7, to compare directly with beta7_v6, which lost about 4% of primes without the threshold.
Replaces the recursive domination votes with the one-line formula vote(p) = (313/p)^3, which is possible now that AND gates removed the dynamic-range limit.
vote(p) = (313/p)^10: exponent 3 failed on neighbouring prime triples, and the tightest triple 41*43*47 needs at least 9. Tests a one-line vote rule at the cost of weights near 1e22.
Fixes v18's two errors, 281*283 and 311*313: their votes differ by only 0.066, so the 0.25 copy vote tipped a digit. COPY_EPS lowered to 0.01.
Replaces the 3-ReLU bumps with one triangle wave per prime, 2 ReLUs per multiple: f_p need not be exactly 0 off multiples because the thresholded AND ignores values below 0.5.
Heads read each digit as a number and W_o holds only 10^i mod p, 325 entries instead of a 2900-entry residue table; S_p has a wider range, so the triangle waves need more kinks.
Block 1's MLP bends S_p into its flag in place, with the residual connection supplying the wave's initial slope: removes the 65 FLAG dimensions and one kink per prime.
Shrinks attention: the 5 place heads in block 1 use a single dimension each, and the 10-dimensional copy head moves to its own attention in block 2.
Replaces the triangle waves with repeated reflection: one ReLU per fold via the residual, x + (2 relu(c-x) - c) = |x-c|, so each prime needs about log2(multiples) folds across MLP blocks.
The last MLP has one unit per distinct digit of each prime, open at every position where that digit appears, instead of one unit per position.
Ties logits to the token dimensions, removing 10 dimensions. Embeddings are scaled to 2^-10 so the input token cannot outweigh the 0.01 copy vote, and W_v rescales them.
Tests the hand-derived claim that exponent 9 is the smallest power law that works, the tightest case being 41*43*47.
Binary priority votes 2^(64-index): each prime outweighs all larger primes combined, so no number-theoretic argument about prime triples is needed.
Last-MLP gates use unit gain, relu(pos_t - |x_p - target|), as non-multiples are at least 1 from the target; binary votes guarantee a margin of 0.5, so COPY_EPS returns to 0.25.
Restores gate gain 2: unit gain failed in v29 because attention leak at distance exactly 1 activated units whose votes reach 2^64. Keeps COPY_EPS at 0.25, now safe with binary votes.
Sensitivity test on the folding circuit: BETA=3, an attention score of 9, compared with the score of 16 at BETA=4.
Sensitivity test on the folding circuit: BETA=3.5, an attention score of 12.25, bracketing the threshold between the failing BETA=3 and the exact BETA=4.
Ablation at BETA=4: copy weight set to 0, to confirm the digit copy is what answers the prime inputs.
Ablation: all votes equal, to measure how often the binary priority is what picks the smallest divisor.
Binary votes restored. Uses plain unsigned 10^i mod p: S_p spans a wider range, but folds grow only logarithmically, so the simpler coefficients may be worth it.
Signed residues restored (unsigned cost one more block). Each MLP is wired to the dimensions it uses: fold MLPs touch only RES; the last reads POS_OUT and RES and writes logits.
Encodes position as a place (t mod 5) plus an output flag, 6 dimensions instead of 11. Keys subtract the flag to exclude output positions, and the constant BIAS dimension goes.
Drops the embedding of position 10: generating 5 answer digits needs only 10 input tokens, so the 11th position is never used. A crash here would mean the evaluator feeds all 11.
Gate gain 4 at BETA=3: tests whether a wider dead zone rescues the soft attention that scored 0.83 at gain 2 in beta3_v31.
Final circuit. Attention is wired like the MLPs: q and k read positions, v reads tokens, W_o writes RES or logits, so every connection in the network is declared.
